research.website_note: The homepage and company pages on transistor.fm identify the site as Transistor's podcast hosting platform.

strategy.observation: Transistor hosts branded podcasts from Kit.com, demonstrating an existing connection to the sender’s target market of B2B brands.
strategy.offer_link: A referral partnership could let Transistor connect B2B brand customers who want production help with podcast audio editing and show notes, complementing its hosting service rather than asking Transistor to buy editing for itself.
hypotheses: Some of Transistor’s B2B brand customers may want outside help editing episodes and preparing show notes.
The Partnerships Lead may consider service-provider referrals that complement Transistor’s hosting offering.
Transistor may not already have a preferred production partner covering this need.
strategy.angle: With Transistor hosting branded shows from Kit.com, would an editing and show-notes referral partner be useful for B2B customers who want production help?
strategy.fit_reason: The service complements podcast hosting and serves a customer segment represented on Transistor’s platform; the Partnerships Lead is a plausible contact for a referral arrangement, though customer demand and partnership appetite are unconfirmed.

draft.subject: Production referrals for B2B podcasts
draft.body:
Hi there,

I noticed Transistor hosts branded shows from Kit.com. If other B2B customers are looking for help with episode production, there may be a fit for a referral partnership.

I provide podcast audio editing and show notes for B2B brands. The idea would be to give customers somewhere to turn for that work alongside their hosting, rather than add production work to your team.

Do you already have a preferred partner for B2B customers who ask for editing and show-notes help?
